title: Proactive prefix scouting and conservative TTL guard for KV cache economics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We lack an automated, low-risk surface for recommending TTL and cache-key changes that consistently reduce per-token cost across tenants without causing latency regressions or cache churn. Existing tooling produces ad-hoc suggestions that engineers must manually validate; this is slow and error-prone.

Goal: Build a 'prefix scout' pipeline that (1) scores candidate prefix families by likely hit-rate lift and cost delta, (2) synthesizes conservative TTL/policy recommendations and cache-key adjustments, and (3) provides a safe apply/rollback flow (shadow analysis, canary, guardrails and automated revert). The system should prioritize low-regret actions and make suggestions actionable for runtime teams and SRE.

Scope: Prefix-level scoring, TTL suggestion generation, safe-apply orchestration, dashboard for review, integration with rollout APIs. Not in scope: model-level codegen changes or customer prompts sanitization (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria: Prefix scoring pipeline produces a ranked list of candidate prefix families with estimated hit-rate delta and cost impact for 90% of production routes
Automated TTL suggestions include recommended TTL, confidence score, and a rationale (sampled prefix traffic distribution and estimated savings)
Safe-apply flow: shadow simulation -> 1% canary on dedicated capacity -> 10% ramp -> full rollout with automatic rollback on defined SLO breaches
Docs and console UI: reviewers can inspect scoring inputs, run notebook to reproduce estimates, and trigger rollout from the console
Integration test: controlled experiment shows net cost savings >= 6% on a selected cohort without P99 latency regression > 5%
design_notes: Scoring model: combination of empirical hit-sampled estimator + Bayesian shrinkage to avoid overconfident uplift for low-volume prefixes
Key features: frequency histogram per prefix, inter-arrival distribution, sequence length conditionality, and coalesced key fingerprints
TTL suggestion heuristic: base on expected marginal hit probability over TTL window multiplied by token cost; prefer conservative values (rounded down to nearest safe bucket: 30s, 2m, 5m, 15m, 1h)
Cache-key design guidance: prefer prefix canonicalization rules that remove volatile suffix tokens and use deterministic joiners; provide regex-based rule templates in the suggestion output
Safety-first defaults: min confidence threshold 0.65 to consider automated apply; suggestions below threshold land in 'needs review' queue
implementation_plan: Data ingest: extend existing sampling pipeline to emit prefix histograms and inter-arrival time distributions (two-week sliding window)
Modeling: implement Bayesian hit uplift estimator and cost-impact calculator in a standalone notebook (python/pandas) and a production scorer (Go service)
UI/UX: add 'Prefix Scout' review page in Console with diff view, rationale, and links to reproduction notebook
Rollout: wire recommendations into rollout service with new 'kv-ttl-safe-apply' orchestration (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> observe -> finalize)
Testing: unit tests for scoring math, e2e tests on canary harness, and synthetic traffic replay for worst-case churn scenarios
rollout_plan: Shadow analysis: apply TTL changes to traffic stream in shadow mode for 48 hours and collect predicted hit delta and latency delta
Small canary: roll recommended TTL to 1% of traffic (isolated cohort) for 4 hours; monitor hit-rate, P95/P99, and error rates
Staged ramp: progress to 10% for 6 hours and re-evaluate; if SLOs remain within thresholds, continue to 50% then 100%
Automated rollback triggers: P99 latency increase > 5%, error rate spike > 1% absolute, or observed cost increase in tokens > 2% vs baseline
Manual checkpoint: any suggestion touching a premium customer route requires manual approval before canary
monitoring_signals: P95/P99 request latency for affected routes
token consumption delta and cost estimate per minute
error and 5xx counts for canary nodes
cache eviction rate and churn metric (new key inserts / minute)
risk_mitigation: Conservative defaults and discrete TTL buckets minimize tuning noise
Use empirical shrinkage to avoid large TTL increases for low-volume prefixes
Shadowing allows us to validate model prediction without impacting production
Rate-limit concurrent automated applies to avoid correlated cache churn across many routes
Rollback automation reduces mean time to revert in case of regressions
notes: Early simulation on a controlled tenant cohort with 30 high-volume prefixes showed estimated cost reduction of ~8% with confidence intervals [5%, 11%]. Sampling bias: 3 of 30 prefixes were long-tail and contributed noisy uplift estimates; model shrinkage corrected those. Next step: expand to broader 100-prefix sample and run full shadow for 48h.
